descriptive_memo.description: 400-800 word narrative describing what the DATA shows. Write in conceptual present tense using gerunds. Use participants' language. Include variation: 'in some cases... in others...'. Do not force a conditions/consequences structure if the data does not support it.

what_emerged.description: 3-5 key findings consolidated across paradigm iterations. Each entry describes a pattern that solidified, including when it appeared and what incidents support it.

items.description: A single finding: 'Finding N — pattern consolidated across iterations, with evidence note.'

what_remains_open.description: Unresolved questions — properties or dimensions that need more evidence to be fully documented.

items.description: A single open question: 'Open question — what remains to be documented and why.'

evolution_narrative.description: How the category definition evolved across paradigm iterations: version 1 → version 2 → ... → version N. Describe what changed at each iteration and why (which incident or expansion drove the change).

representative_incidents.description: Maximum 3 incidents that best represent the category. Select incidents that show variation or critical turning points.

text.description: The incident text (verbatim quote or close paraphrase from the segment).

why.description: Why this incident is representative: what pattern, dimension, or variation it exemplifies.
